# LUMO.md
<!-- Auto-maintained by Lumo. Do not edit manually. -->

## Traps

- When you run the Day 1 test script (scripts/test-lumo-proposal.ts) without a real task context from the database, the LLM client will receive an incomplete or mocked memory list. The generateProposal call may succeed but produce operations that reference non-existent memory IDs, or the prompt will show example data instead of real task memories. Workaround: Use scripts/test-lumo-proposal.ts to fetch a real task from the database (via taskRepository.findForMemoryContext), retrieve its actual memories, and pass that full context to generateProposal. Verify the returned operations reference real memory IDs from that task. <!-- from: LUM-36 -->
- If a user clicks Sync to LUMO.md twice in quick succession before the first proposal is applied, the system may create two separate proposals from the same task memory state. Both proposals are saved to the database with status PENDING. When the user applies the first one, it opens a PR. When they apply the second, it may create a duplicate PR or conflict with the first if LUMO.md has already been modified. Workaround: After calling generateProposal, immediately disable the Sync button on the frontend until the user either confirms and applies the proposal or dismisses the preview modal. Check in the sync endpoint that the proposal status is still PENDING before proceeding; reject with a clear error if it has already been applied. <!-- from: LUM-36 -->
- If you attempt to apply a LUMO.md proposal when the proposal record has already been applied (status is not PENDING), the sync endpoint will process the same operations twice. The system creates a duplicate PR with the same entries added again, or errors if the branch already exists. Workaround: Before applying the operations in the sync endpoint, check that the proposal status is PENDING. Reject the request with a clear error message if the proposal has already been applied. On the frontend, after the first successful sync, disable the Sync button or display a link to the existing PR instead of allowing a second sync attempt. <!-- from: LUM-36 -->
## Decisions

- LUMO.md is auto-generated from Layer 1 task memory (TRAP, DECISION, CONVENTION, PROCEDURAL entries) only, without incorporating other sources like project description or sprint goals. This focused approach establishes a clear contract between what agents record and what users see, and avoids the complexity of reconciling multiple independent sources. Future iterations can extend the source set once the memory-only pipeline is stable and proven. <!-- from: LUM-36 -->
- LUMO.md generation is triggered at task granularity, not project granularity — each task completion generates an incremental proposal against the current LUMO.md using only that task's memory entries. This provides better traceability (every LUMO.md change can be traced back to the task that introduced it) and makes the proposal workflow simpler. Project-level generation would require deduplication and conflict resolution logic across all tasks, adding complexity. <!-- from: LUM-36 -->
- LUMO.md proposals are persisted to the database in a `LumoProposal` model with status (pending/applied/rejected), rather than generated as ephemeral outputs. This provides proposal auditability, recall for the PR workflow, and coordination about which proposals have already been integrated. The model stores the generated operations, status, source task_id, timestamps, and rejection reason. <!-- from: LUM-36 -->
- LUMO.md proposals operate at entry granularity, where each operation targets a single memory entry (TRAP, DECISION, CONVENTION, or PROCEDURAL row) rather than whole sections or free-form text. This provides precise traceability: every change in LUMO.md can be mapped back to the exact memory row that generated it. The LumoProposal model stores a list of operations, each with a type (ADD / UPDATE / DELETE / SUPERSEDE), a memory entry ID, and the new content. <!-- from: LUM-36 -->
- LUMO.md uses structured format with YAML frontmatter metadata on each entry rather than pure Markdown, to enable programmatic parsing and entry-level operations. The generation utility emits structured metadata (e.g. YAML frontmatter or HTML comments with memory row IDs) alongside each entry so the system can map LUMO.md content back to source memory rows. The markdown remains human-readable because narrative content lives in plain text; metadata is minimal and non-intrusive. <!-- from: LUM-36 -->
- LUMO.md proposal generation uses a single-call LLM strategy (one generateObject() call) to produce proposals from task memories, rather than a multi-stage pipeline. The LLM sees both the task's memories and the current LUMO.md simultaneously, so it can naturally handle deduplication and conflict detection in one shot. This aligns with the established sprint-summary-client.ts pattern already in use. Output quality depends entirely on prompt engineering; if proposals become unreliable, the team may revisit a two-stage approach. <!-- from: LUM-36 -->
- LUMO.md proposal operations use a discriminated union schema where each operation type (ADD / UPDATE / DELETE / SUPERSEDE) has a separate sub-schema with only its required fields, eliminating optional fields that could be ambiguous. The Zod schema uses z.discriminatedUnion('type', [...]) and lets the type system enforce that each operation has exactly the fields it needs. This makes the LLM's output schema clearer and reduces iteration cycles. <!-- from: LUM-36 -->
- LUMO.md proposals are applied using line-level string operations on pure Markdown, without an AST parser, to keep implementation simple and readable. Since each entry is a single bullet line with metadata (<!-- from: LUM-{id} -->), string matching and line replacement are sufficient to locate and modify individual entries. If entries grow more complex (e.g. nested structures or multi-line content), the line-based approach may need to evolve. <!-- from: LUM-36 -->
- The 'Sync to LUMO.md' button is placed on the Task detail page, so each task can generate and apply its own memory-to-markdown proposals independently. This task-granular placement is the most direct and discoverable for the demo workflow and aligns with the existing task-granular proposal design. Project-level or bulk-sync features may be added in future iterations. <!-- from: LUM-36 -->
- The Sync to LUMO.md workflow uses a preview-then-confirm flow: a modal displays the specific entries being added, updated, superseded, or deleted before the user approves the sync. This additional friction is justified because correctness and auditability matter more than raw speed. The preview is the last opportunity to catch errors before bad commits. <!-- from: LUM-36 -->
- The Sync to LUMO.md workflow uses a two-call API architecture: the frontend first calls POST /api/tasks/[id]/lumo-proposals to generate and preview the proposal, then calls POST /api/lumo-proposals/[proposalId]/sync to apply it and create the PR. This decouples generation from application, allowing the preview step to block before any Git changes occur. It reuses the existing generateProposal service, leverages the GitHub Git Data API (which supports multi-file operations), and preserves proposal records in the database for audit trails. <!-- from: LUM-36 -->
- The team uses the GitHub Git Data API (rather than REST API or local git) for creating PRs, because it supports multi-file operations in a single commit — critical for Day 4 onboarding, where the system must create LUMO.md and simultaneously update CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md with @import directives. It avoids cloning the repo or managing local git state, and integrates cleanly with the existing backend service layer. <!-- from: LUM-36 -->
- Duplicate Sync operations are detected by checking the database for an existing PENDING or APPLIED proposal from the same task, rather than making a real-time GitHub API call to verify the PR is still open. This is fast and gives immediate feedback; for v0, it is acceptable to rely on the proposal record as the source of truth. The sync endpoint records which proposal ID was applied to which PR for future correlation. <!-- from: LUM-36 -->
- Git merge conflicts arising from simultaneous open PRs will not be detected or resolved by the system; instead, they will be surfaced to the user in GitHub's native PR review interface for manual resolution. The system always reads the latest LUMO.md from the default branch before applying, so conflicts only occur if two PRs are open simultaneously and both modify LUMO.md. The team deferred conflict handling to GitHub's standard workflow until users report conflicts as a regular pain point. <!-- from: LUM-36 -->
- The LUMO.md sync-to-PR feature design was documented as a comprehensive specification (2026-05-12-lumo-sync-pr.md) to align the implementation roadmap across Day 1 and Day 2 subagents. The specification ensures both teams understand the API contract, operation types, error handling, and data flows before they diverge into implementation. Any deviation during implementation requires updating the spec first and confirming with the team. <!-- from: LUM-36 -->
## Conventions

- System prompts and user prompts for LLM calls must be written in English, while generated content (like LUMO.md entries) should reflect the project's own language. The convention ensures stable LLM reasoning and structured output quality. If the project's CLAUDE.md and memory entries are in Chinese or another language, the generated content will naturally follow that language; the English-language prompts only govern the instruction layer, not the output content. <!-- from: LUM-36 -->
- Task-related API endpoints use `[id]` as the route parameter (e.g. POST /api/tasks/[id]/lumo-proposals), not `[taskId]`, for consistency with existing project patterns. This convention applies to all task-scoped routes to maintain a uniform mental model across the codebase. <!-- from: LUM-36 -->
## Procedures

- How to set up the Layer 2 (LUMO.md generation) pipeline: (1) Create a memory-to-markdown utility that reads all non-deleted rows from the memory table, grouped by category (TRAP / DECISION / CONVENTION / PROCEDURAL). (2) For each category, format the entries as a markdown section with a headline and readable narrative. (3) Store or write the generated LUMO.md to the repo root (or a configurable path specified in user settings). (4) Wire this generation to trigger on CREATE, UPDATE, DELETE operations in the memory repository. Consider debouncing if many updates happen in quick succession. (5) Ensure CLAUDE.md already contains an @import directive or similar mechanism to load LUMO.md so Claude Code agents see it when they start work. <!-- from: LUM-36 -->
- How to apply LUMO.md proposal operations by parsing and modifying the markdown file: (1) Split LUMO.md into lines. Identify section headings by looking for lines that start with `##`, which mark the beginning of each category section (TRAP, DECISION, CONVENTION, PROCEDURAL). (2) For each section, the content extends from the heading line to the next heading line (or end of file). Entries are stored as bullet list items: `- {narrative content} <!-- from: LUM-{number} -->`. (3) For an ADD operation: find the target section heading. Append a new bullet line at the end of that section with the entry content and metadata comment. If the section does not exist, create it at the end of the file. (4) For an UPDATE operation: locate the bullet line in the target section that contains the old content. Replace that line with the new content while preserving the `<!-- from: -->` metadata comment. (5) For a DELETE operation: find and remove the bullet line containing the entry from its section. If the section becomes empty, remove the section heading as well. (6) Write the modified LUMO.md back to disk. <!-- from: LUM-36 -->
- How to check whether a repository is onboarded to Layer 2 (LUMO.md generation): (1) Check whether {repoPath}/LUMO.md exists. (2) Check whether {repoPath}/CLAUDE.md exists, and if it does, verify that it contains an @import directive for LUMO.md. (3) Check whether {repoPath}/AGENTS.md exists, and if it does, verify that it contains an @import directive for LUMO.md. (4) Return a status object with flags: lumoMdExists (boolean), claudeMdImported (boolean), agentsMdExists (boolean), agentsMdImported (boolean). <!-- from: LUM-36 -->
- How to guide a user through onboarding when LUMO.md or @import directives are missing: (1) If LUMO.md does not exist or is not imported, display a dialog listing the missing setup steps. (2) Offer the user a choice to add @import LUMO.md to CLAUDE.md, to AGENTS.md, or to both files. (3) Once the user confirms, programmatically insert the @import LUMO.md directive into the selected file(s). (4) After setup completes, allow the user to proceed with the memory sync operation. <!-- from: LUM-36 -->
- How to write tests for the LUMO.md proposal generation pipeline: (1) Create a script test (`scripts/test-lumo-proposal.ts`) that reads a real task's memories from the database, mocks LUMO.md content, and calls `generateProposal` to verify the returned operations match the expected schema and rationale is meaningful. (2) Write unit tests for `lumo-proposal.prompt.ts` to verify that the prompt constructor produces correctly formatted output with complete task and memory information. (3) Write unit tests for `lumo-proposal.repository.ts` covering CRUD operations against the LumoProposal model using mocked Prisma calls. (4) Write unit tests for `applyProposal` with line-level operation logic: given LUMO.md content and a list of operations (ADD, UPDATE, DELETE), verify the output file content is correct, including adding to existing sections, creating new sections, and removing entries. (5) Do not write automated tests for raw LLM output quality — that is a prompt-iteration concern, not a unit test concern. Instead, validate schema compliance and structural correctness. <!-- from: LUM-36 -->
- How to integrate the LumoProposal model and repository into the task's existing deletion cascade: (1) Check that the Prisma schema LumoProposal model has `@relation(onDelete: Cascade)` on the Task foreign key so Postgres automatically deletes all LumoProposal rows when the Task is deleted. (2) If the application provides a Task deletion service (e.g. task.service.ts or task.repository.ts), ensure it calls the LumoProposal repository cleanup or relies on the Postgres cascade. Do not manually delete proposals unless your database does not support cascading deletes. (3) Run a test to confirm: delete a task with existing proposals and verify that the proposals are also removed from the database. <!-- from: LUM-36 -->
- How to document a LUMO.md sync feature design as a specification: (1) Create a markdown design spec file in docs/superpowers/specs/ with a date prefix (e.g., 2026-05-12-lumo-sync-pr-design.md). (2) Structure the spec with sections covering: overview (problem statement and scope), API contract (endpoint paths with request/response shapes), user workflow (preview-then-confirm flow), backend architecture (service layers and Git Data API integration), and error handling (duplicate sync detection, merge conflicts, GitHub auth failures). (3) Reference existing task memories (DECISION and PROCEDURAL entries) by their IDs so future readers can trace design rationale. (4) Document assumptions (e.g. merge conflicts surfaced in GitHub's native PR review). (5) Include terminal interactions or pseudocode showing example API request/response payloads and operation sequences. (6) Stage the spec file and commit it to the repository with a clear commit message. <!-- from: LUM-36 -->
- How to implement the GitHub Tree Service layer for LUMO.md sync operations: (1) Create `lib/services/lumo-sync/github-tree.service.ts` with three core methods: `readFile(owner, repo, path, token)`, `createBranchWithFiles(owner, repo, baseBranch, newBranchName, files, token)`, and `createPullRequest(owner, repo, title, head, base, body, token)`. (2) `readFile` should call the GitHub REST API to fetch file content from the default branch, returning null if the file does not exist. (3) `createBranchWithFiles` should atomically create a new branch and commit multiple files via the Git Data API: fetch the base branch reference, create a new tree with the updated files, create a commit on that tree, and update the reference to point to the new commit. (4) `createPullRequest` should call the GitHub REST API to create a PR pointing the new branch (head) to the default branch (base), returning the PR URL and PR number. (5) All methods accept a GitHub authentication token parameter and include it in the Authorization header for API calls. (6) Test the service with unit tests that mock the GitHub API responses and verify correct request construction and error handling. <!-- from: LUM-36 -->
- How to implement the LUMO.md sync service that orchestrates the full proposal-to-PR workflow: (1) Create `lib/services/lumo-sync/lumo-sync.service.ts` with a core `sync(proposalId: string, userId: string, workspaceId: string)` method that returns `{ prUrl, prNumber, branchName }`. (2) Inside sync, load the proposal record from the database and verify its status is PENDING. Throw an error if the proposal is already APPLIED or REJECTED. (3) Query the GitHubIntegration table using userId and workspaceId to retrieve the user's GitHub OAuth token. If no integration exists, throw a user-friendly error. (4) Load the Project record using proposal.projectId to retrieve the GitHub repository owner, repo name, and default branch. (5) Call githubTreeService.readFile(owner, repo, 'LUMO.md', token) to fetch the current LUMO.md content. If the file does not exist, treat the content as empty. (6) Apply the proposal's stored operations (from proposal.operations) to the fetched LUMO.md content in-memory, generating the new file content. (7) Call githubTreeService.createBranchWithFiles(owner, repo, defaultBranch, newBranchName, files, token) where files includes the updated LUMO.md. If Day 4 onboarding is needed, include CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md with @import directives in the same commit. (8) Call githubTreeService.createPullRequest(owner, repo, title, newBranchName, defaultBranch, body, token) to open the PR. (9) Update the proposal record in the database: set status to APPLIED, store the PR URL and PR number returned from the API, record the appliedAt timestamp and branch name. (10) Return `{ prUrl, prNumber, branchName }` to the caller. <!-- from: LUM-36 -->
- How to implement the two-endpoint API flow for LUMO.md proposal preview and synchronization: (1) Define POST /api/tasks/[id]/lumo-proposals: accepts taskId in URL (as [id]), optional currentLumoMd in request body (if not provided, backend fetches from GitHub), calls generateProposal service, saves LumoProposal record with status PENDING, returns `{ id, operations, summary }` to the frontend. (2) Define POST /api/lumo-proposals/[proposalId]/sync: accepts proposalId in URL, loads the proposal from the database, calls lumoSyncService.sync(proposalId, userId, workspaceId), returns `{ prUrl, prNumber, branchName }` on success. (3) Ensure the proposal ID from generateProposal matches the URL parameter in the sync endpoint so the frontend can chain the calls seamlessly after user confirmation. (4) In the sync endpoint, verify the proposal status is PENDING before proceeding; return a clear error if it has already been applied or is missing. (5) Document both endpoints with their authentication requirements (userId from session, GitHub token validation), error cases (file conflicts, GitHub API failures, missing GitHub integration), and the schema of each request/response. <!-- from: LUM-36 -->
